title: refactor(tool-exec): ergonomic multi-tool orchestration, result injection, and retry semantics
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: users building complex tool chains requested clearer ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool calls (particularly when mixing streaming LLM output and tool result injection), more predictable retry semantics for transient tool runner failures, and a path toward OpenAI-compat structured output envelopes. This PR refactors the tool execution API surface to: 1) introduce a high-level ToolExecutionPlan that expresses ordered or parallel tool groups (supports per-tool concurrency hints), 2) add explicit injection_points that let the runtime insert structured tool result envelopes into the streamed token sequence with stable delimiter tokens, and 3) add idempotency keys + exponential jittered retry helpers for tool runners plus a coordinator-level retry policy that avoids double-execution for side-effectful tools. Changes are backward-compatible by default: the previous single-tool call path remains supported. Key behaviors: - Parallel groups: the planner can execute non-dependent tools in parallel and stream their results as interleaved structured envelopes; ordering is preserved inside each tool. - Injection points: callers can specify where tool outputs should appear relative to assistant messages (before/after/specific-token anchors). Runtime emits a consistent JSONL envelope ("__tool_result__" token marker) that SDKs can hydrate into structured_output items. - Retries: each tool execution gets an idempotency_key; coordinator will not retry tools marked non-idempotent. Retries use configurable backoff with randomized jitter and a max_attempts cap. - OpenAI-compat: compatibility layer extended with new fields (tool_concurrency, injection_points, structured_output_v1) and translation helpers for older client requests. Implementation summary: - Core: refactor tool_orchestrator (pkg/runtime/orchestrator) to a planner/executor split. - Protocol: introduce tool_execution_plan.proto and structured_result.proto for wire-stable envelopes. - Streaming: update streaming multiplexer to recognize tool envelope markers and avoid buffering assistant tokens while waiting for parallel tool results (reduces stalls). - SDK: client-side helpers in redwood-sdk-typescript to build plans and to parse injected structured_output envelopes; updated examples. - Tests: unit coverage for parallel scheduling, injection ordering, and idempotency logic; integration test that replays a previously flaky golden stream (reproduced in perf-canary). Risks and mitigations: - Streaming order complexity: added end-to-end integration test and a new stream fuzzer that exercises interleaving; watchdog will force fallback to sequential group execution on detection of malformed envelopes. - Backwards compatibility: compatibility translators inserted early in request pipeline; maintained default behavior. Checklist: - [x] planner/executor split implemented - [x] structured envelopes defined and stable - [x] SDK helpers in TS added - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + migration notes drafted - [x] perf canary run (green) Related: ENG-3421 (tooling ergonomics), ENG-3560 (streaming stability).

review_comments: Luis Moreno (review): This is a large surface change — can we ensure we have a clear migration path for existing single-tool callers? Suggest adding a compatibility translator unit test.
Priya Kaur (author): Added compat_translator.go and unit test; kept old single-tool handler on by default. See added test: test/unit/compat/single_tool_compat.test.go.

Asha Patel (review): Concern about streaming: if two parallel tools emit many small chunks, will we interleave them in a way that breaks existing streaming parsers? Recommend a distinct token marker and an opt-in flag for early rollout.

Priya Kaur (author): Implemented __tool_result__ JSONL envelope token and added opt-in header X-Redwood-Tool-Injection to gate injection until SDKs can be rolled out. Also added stream fuzzer and an integration test that simulates many small chunks.
Tom Bernard (review): Please add metrics for dropped/invalid envelopes and a canary run. Also double-check telemetry does not leak tool outputs in non-PII-safe logs.
Priya Kaur (author): Added tool_execution_metrics and masked tool payloads in observability layer; triggered a perf-canary run (see CI comments).
release_notes: Introduce ToolExecutionPlan to express parallel/ordered tool groups, injection_points for deterministic streamed tool result insertion (JSONL __tool_result__ envelopes), coordinator-level retry policy with idempotency keys, and OpenAI-compatibility translations for tool_concurrency and structured_output_v1. Backwards-compatible by default; SDK updates available in typescript package.
notes: This PR touches runtime, protocol, SDK and docs. We intentionally kept the default behavior unchanged and gated injection behind an opt-in header to reduce risk during rollout. Perf canary showed median latency unchanged and tail latency improved for mixed tool/LLM workloads.
